summary: 78-year-old man on apixaban with 2 days of visible haematuria and clots, now in retention (850 mL with clot), Hb 10.8 from 13.2.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Blood clots in the urine and now cannot pass water
inputs.hpi: Atrial fibrillation on apixaban. Two days of heavy red urine with clots; unable to pass urine for 6 hours with painful lower abdomen. No trauma, no catheter history. GP had assumed the bleeding was "from the blood thinner".

exam.general: Pale, distressed. Pulse 104/min irregular, BP 132/80, RR 18, temperature 36.8°C.
exam.abdomen: Tender palpable bladder. PR: smooth moderately enlarged prostate.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Clot retention from visible haematuria on apixaban
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Clot retention with visible haematuria on apixaban; 3-way catheter and irrigation; haematuria still needs full investigation (cystoscopy, CT urogram).

mustInclude.note: Haematuria on anticoagulation is investigated the same way; the anticoagulant does not explain it.
Standard practice for clot retention; not a specific guideline statement.
mustInclude.knownGapNote: Web: No three-way catheter or irrigation; a standard Foley is suggested.

guideline.name: EAU Guidelines on Non-muscle-invasive Bladder Cancer (diagnosis)
guideline.section: Visible haematuria: cystoscopy and upper tract imaging (CT urography); haematuria in patients on anticoagulant or antiplatelet treatment is investigated in the same way
guideline.citation: Gontero P, Birtle A, Compérat E, et al. EAU Guidelines on Non-muscle-invasive Bladder Cancer (TaT1 and CIS). EAU Guidelines Office, Arnhem; 2024 edition.

guideline.name: NICE NG12 — Suspected cancer: recognition and referral
guideline.section: Urological cancers: refer using a suspected cancer pathway (2-week wait) for bladder or kidney cancer if aged ≥45 with unexplained visible haematuria without urinary tract infection, or visible haematuria that persists or recurs after successful treatment of UTI; suspected spinal metastases in people with cancer
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Suspected cancer: recognition and referral. NICE guideline NG12. London: NICE; 2015 (updated).

guideline.name: EAU Guidelines on the management of non-neurogenic male LUTS (acute urinary retention)
guideline.section: Acute urinary retention: bladder decompression by urethral (or suprapubic) catheter; alpha-blocker before trial without catheter; renal function; identify precipitants (anticholinergics, constipation)
guideline.citation: Gravas S, Gacci M, Gratzke C, et al. EAU Guidelines on Management of Non-Neurogenic Male LUTS. EAU Guidelines Office, Arnhem; 2024 edition.

rationale: Clot retention needs catheter drainage; anticoagulation does not explain visible haematuria, so it is still investigated (EAU NMIBC, NICE NG12).
